minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Agency,
  Community Development Financing Authority,
  Public Improvement Corporation,
  and Library Board of Trustees*

  November 16, 2009

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Agency, the Community
Development Financing Authority, the Public Improvement Corporation, and the Library Board
of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Ury at 5:03
p.m., on November 16, 2009 at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on November 12, 2009, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Ledesma
  Council Member Schlicht
  Mayor Pro Tem MacLean (arrived at 5:14 p.m.)
  Mayor Ury

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Irwin B. Bornstein, Assistant City Manager/Director of Admin. Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Ledesma

INVOCATION: Council Member Kelley

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Real Property Negotiator pursuant to Government Code Section
  54956.8. Real property denoted as Parcel 2 of Tentative Tract Map No. 16877, with

City Council Minutes  1  November 16, 2009
   a common address of 25565 Los Alisos Boulevard, Mission Viejo, California and
  generally situated easterly of the intersection of Jeronimo Road and Los Alisos
  Boulevard in the City of Mission Viejo owned by Target Corporation. CDA
  Negotiators: Dennis Wilberg, City Manager/CDA Executive Director, Charles
  Wilson, Director of Community Development, James Williams, Economic Advisor,
  Celeste Brady, CDA Counsel, and William Curley, III, City Attorney. Negotiating
  Parties: CDA Negotiators on behalf of Community Development Agency of the City
  of Mission Viejo; and Bob Garrison Lennar Homes as prospective buyer from
  Target Corporation; Roger Grable of Manatt Phelps, counsel to Lennar; Julie
  Rosenbaum of Target Corporation; Michele Jefcoat of CBRE, broker for subject
  property. Under negotiation: Potential acquisition and/or disposition of real
  property interests for long term affordable housing and the price and terms of
  payment therefor related to the above-listed Property. Factors Affecting Price and
  Terms under Negotiation: Recorded covenants, Scope of development of Property,
  and Affordable housing requirements. Factors affecting time of payment:
  Conditions to closing, Due diligence period, and Schedule of performance and
  Development of Affordable Housing.

CS2. Conference with City Attorney Concerning One matter of Existing Litigation
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(a). The Litigation is City of Mission
  Viejo v. CUSD, Case No. 00180049; Companion Case, Rancho Santa Margarita v.
  CUSD, Case No. 00207543.

CS3. Conference with City Attorney Concerning One matter of Existing Litigation
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(a). The Litigation is City of Mission
  Viejo v. Saddleback Valley Unified School District (SVUSD), Case No. 00300610.

CS4. Conference with Legal Counsel -- Anticipated Litigation. Potential Litigation
  Pursuant to Subdivision (c) of Government Code Section 54956.9. Two Cases Under
  Consideration.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:05 p.m., Mayor Ury declared a recess to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:07 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that for Closed Session items CS1, CS2 and CS3 the
council gave direction but there was no reportable action. For item CS4, he provided an update
on one potential litigation matter and the other matter will be addressed as part of open session
item number 24.

City Council Minutes  2  November 16, 2009
 PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Community of Character Award

  Mayor Ury, Crime Prevention Specialist Tammy Descoteaux and youth Committee
  Member Amanda Gordon presented the Community of Character Award to Jim
  Humphries, Exhalted Ruler of Mission Viejo Elks Lodge #2444.

P2.  Community of Character Award

  Mayor Ury, Crime Prevention Specialist Tammy Descoteaux and youth Committee
  Member Francis Vu presented the Community of Character Award to the Mission Viejo
  Nadadores CHOC Swimmers.

P3.  Presentation by the County on the Status of the Environmental Efforts for the La
  Pata Avenue Gap Closure and Del Rio Extension Project

  Les Card of LSA Associates, representing the County of Orange Public Works
  Department, provided information on the County’s initiation of the La Pata Avenue Gap
  Closure and the Del Rio Extension. This proposed project would implement a gap
  closure by constructing four new lanes from Ortega Highway at the landfill, south to
  Calle Saluda and Avenida La Pata in San Clemente.

John Schatz, General Manager of Santa Margarita Water District, provided an update on the
algae bloom odor at Upper Oso Reservoir. He presented photos of the prior and present
conditions of the water at the reservoir and invited residents to attend the next SMWD Board
Meeting on Wednesday, November 18, 2009, at 7:00 p.m.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Dr. Scott Wilbur, Principal of Carl Hankey School, IB Coordinator Chris Grantz and Assistant
Principal Greg Hauser, M.V.: announced the International Baccalaureate (IB) Program at Carl
Hankey Elementary School and the "Hawk Trot" fundraiser on Friday, November 20, 2009.
They announced that British Patroleum has offered to match, dollar for dollar, all funds raised at
the Hawk Trot.

Sharon Cody, M.V.: stated that she’s pleased that a dog park is not being considered for the
animal shelter.

City Council Minutes  3  November 16, 2009
 David Allen, M.V.: announced that the annual Gifts and Goodies Boutique, presented by the
Mission Viejo Activities Committee will be held on Saturday, November 21 from 8:00 a.m. to
5:00 pm at the Murray Community Center. He also reminded residents that Santa Claus will
arrive at Civic Center plaza on Sunday, November 29 at 6:00 p.m. after a holiday celebration that
begins at 3:00 p.m. More information is available at www.mvactivities.com.

Helen Workun, M.V.: announced that the Heritage Committee is now offering the Mission Viejo
History book for $25 and a deck of playing cards for $10. Both are available at city hall, the
library, the Murray Community and Senior Center and they will also be sold at the Gift and
Goddies Boutique this Saturday.

Robert Reidel, M.V.: provided an update on the CUSD trustee election proposal and announced
that the CUSD Board is currently challenging the proposed initiative. He urged the Council to
hold a forum so residents can become more informed on the issues.

Dr. Philip Glaser, Laguna Niguel: as an animal shelter volunteer, he stated that he is a strong
supporter of dog parks but he feels the pet path would be compromised if a dog park were placed
at the Animal Services Center.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Item 15 was removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said
  titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title
  and further reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

City Council Minutes  4  November 16, 2009
   Approved the Minutes for the Regular Meeting of November 2, 2009, as presented.

3.  Check Register dated October 23, 2009, in the amount of $1,025,228.44

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register dated October 30, 2009, in the amount of $2,247,808.46

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Quarterly Check Registers and Quarterly Cash Receipts Report – First Quarter of
  FY 2009-10

  Received and filed.

6.  City Treasurer's Monthly Report for September 2009

  Received and filed.

7.  Community Development Agency Treasurer's Monthly Report for September 2009

  Received and filed.

8.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer’s Monthly Report for September 2009

  Received and filed.

9.  Quarterly Financial Report for the City of Mission Viejo – First Quarter of 2009-10

  Received and filed.

10.  Quarterly Financial Report for the Community Development Agency – First
  Quarter of 2009-10

  Received and filed.

11.  Comprehensive Annual Financial Report for the City of Mission Viejo for the Fiscal
  Year Ended June 30, 2009

City Council Minutes  5  November 16, 2009
   Received and filed.

12.  Water Efficient Landscape Regulations Ordinance

  Adopted Ordinance 09-277 Repealing and Replacing Chapter 8.12 of the Mission Viejo
  Code Entitled, "Water Efficient Landscape Ordinance".

13.  Community Services Funding Program - Funding for Fiscal Year 2009-2010

  Approved the Community Services Commission's recommended funding amounts for
  Fiscal Year 2009-2010 for the Community Services Funding Program.

14.  American Recovery and Reinvestment Act of 2009 (ARRA) Street Rehabilitation
  Project (CIPs 202/837)

  (1) Awarded the construction contract for the subject project to All American Asphalt,
  Inc., in the amount of $1,027,027; and (2) adopted Resolution 09-56 Amending the
Fiscal Year 2009-2010 Budget for Costs Related to CIP 202.

Ed Ewart, South County Outreach, Lake Forest: highlighted the recent Orange County Register
article which outlined their food bank efforts. Thanked the City Council for supporting South
County Outreach (item 13).

STAFF REPORTS

City Attorney’s Report

24.  Response to the Cure and Correct Demand Presented by Resident Karen L.
  Medeiros

  City Attorney Bill Curley presented the staff report and announced that there was no
  Brown Act violation. A document to that effect will be available tomorrow morning
  following the City Council’s direction in Closed Session.

  By consensus, the City Council received and filed the report. A response letter will be
  mailed to Ms. Medeiros and will be available for public viewing in the office of the City
  Clerk.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS

City Council Minutes  6  November 16, 2009
 Council Member Kelley

26.  Dog Park

  The following spoke in support of a dog park, in opposition to the Oso Viejo Park
  location, and expressed an interest in working together to find a new location: Susan
  Sellers, M.V.; Sharon Cody, M.V.; Anna T. Boyce, M.V.; Christa Hattem, M.V.; Lisa
  Moreno, M.V.; Myron Sipp, M.V.; Mary Holley, M.V.; Nora Neumiller, M.V.; Mitch
  Kronowitt, M.V.; Melora Vandersluis, M.V.; and Dave Gove, M.V.

  The following presented written comments in favor of reconsidering the dog park
  location: Christy Welch, M.V.; Dane Kovacs, M.V.; Bonnie Teder, M.V.; and Greg
  Naliboff, M.V.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ledesma, to (1)
  rescind the Council’s prior location decision and assign the approved funding to an
  alternate site; (2) direct staff to look at the residents’ proposals for alternate sites and get
  cost and conceptual work done for the Felipe Arroyo and Lower Curtis Park locations as
  well as any other potential sites; and (3) return this matter to the Community Services
  Commission for review, a public hearing(s) and input from the residents.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  By consensus, the City Council directed staff to return in January 2010 (if possible), to
  proceed with the pass key proposal, and look at the opportunity to use volunteer help to
  move this effort forward.

RECESS

At the hour of 7:32 p.m., Mayor Ury declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 7:50
p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

16.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority Lease Revenue
  Refunding Bonds, 2009 Series A

City Council Minutes  7  November 16, 2009
   Assistant City Manager/Director of Administrative Services Irwin Bornstein presented
  the staff report.

  Mayor Ury opened the public hearing at 7:51 p.m. Upon hearing no comments from
  members of the public, Mayor Ury closed the public hearing at 7:51 p.m.

  Motion made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to (1)
  adopt City of Mission Viejo Resolution 09-57 Approving Proceedings by the Mission
  Viejo Community Development Financing Authority for the Issuance and Sale of Lease
  Revenue Bonds to Refund the Outstanding City of Mission Viejo Certificates of
  Participation (1996 Mission Viejo Public Library Financing Project) and the Outstanding
  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority Lease Revenue Bonds,
  2001 Series A (City Hall Construction and Library Expansion Project), and Approving
  Related Documents and Official Actions; (2) adopt CDFA Resolution 09-03,
  Authorizing the Issuance and Sale of Lease Revenue Bonds to Refund the Outstanding
  City of Mission Viejo Certificates of Participation (1996 Mission Viejo Public Library
  Financing Project) and the outstanding Mission Viejo Community Development
  Financing Authority Lease Revenue bonds, 2001 Series A (City Hall Construction and
  Library Expansion Project), and approving related documents and official actions; and (3)
  adopt PIC Resolution 09-01 Authorizing the Execution and Delivery of a Termination
  Agreement Relating to the Outstanding City of Mission Viejo Certificates of
  Participation (1996 Mission Viejo Public Library Financing Project) and approving
  official actions.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

OLD BUSINESS

17.  Business Registration

  Director of Community Development Chuck Wilson presented the staff report and
  provided the results of the survey and review work.

  By consensus, the City Council received and filed the report.

City Council Minutes  8  November 16, 2009
 MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS

19.  Possible Renaming of Youth Athletic Park to Marty Russo Youth Athletic Park

  Director of Recreation and Community Services presented the staff report.

  The following spoke in support of the re-naming of the park to Marty Russo Youth
  Athletic Park: Robert D. Breton, M.V.; Arthur Cook, M.V.; Peggy Russo, M.V.; Richard
  Fiore, M.V.; Joe Zambito, M.V.; Bob Bunyan, M.V.; and Anthony Accetta, M.V.

  Motion made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Council Member Kelley,
  to approve the Community Services Commission’s recommendation to rename the Youth
  Athletic Park to the Marty Russo Youth Athletic Park.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

NEW BUSINESS

18.  Request for Proposals for Integrated Solid Waste Management Services

  Denise Matson, Senior Management Analyst, presented the staff report.

  Joe Sloan and Enrique Vasquez outlined the RFP development process and what will
  occur going forward.

  By consensus, the City Council directed that this item is brought back at the next meeting
  to give the Council three full weeks to review the RFP and draft agreement and pose any
  questions that may arise during that time. Council Members will provide questions to the
  City Manager by Wednesday, November 25, 2009.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

15.  Shade Canopy Installation over the Bleachers at Various Sports Parks

  Mayor Ury continued this item to next City Council Meeting.

City Council Minutes  9  November 16, 2009
 MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS (Continued)

20.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Council Member Kelley presented the report.

21.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Pro Tem MacLean presented the report.

22.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Ledesma presented the report.

23.  SCAG Transportation & Communications Committee (TCC) Report

  Council Member Kelley presented the report.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS (Continued)

25.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the staff report and agreed to provide any changes to the City
  Clerk for the public record.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley reminded residents of the “Hawk Trot" event which will help raise
funds for the Baccalaureate program at Carl Hankey Elementary School. The fundraiser will be
held on November 20 and more information can be obtained by contacting Hankey School. She
thanked Deputy City Manager Karen Wylie for another wonderful Veteran's Day ceremony and
she announced that she also attended the service in Lake Forest where Mission Viejo participated
by donating flowers in honor of the thirteen victims of the Fort Hood shooting. Council Member
Kelley outlined her attendance at several other recent programs: a foreclosure workshop, the
charter school meeting presented by Oxford Preparatory Academy, and the grand opening of the
new Mission Hospital medical tower. She noted that she was very impressed to learn that
Mission Hospital is now the number one diagnostic center in the world. Council Member Kelley

City Council Minutes  10  November 16, 2009
 announced that she was honored to interview Major Brian Dennis who was here last week
talking about the book he has written, "Nubs: The True Story of a Mutt, a Marine & a Miracle."
Major Dennis' book is an account of his tour of duty in Iraq when he befriended his dog Nubs.
Finally, Council Member Kelley reminded residents of the Santa's arrival event on Sunday,
November 29. Activities begin at 3:00 and Santa will arrive at 6:00 p.m.

Council Member Ledesma

Council Member Ledesma stated that he looks forward to seeing many of the City's residents at
Santa's arrival.

Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht, on behalf of resident Joe Holtzman, acknowledged staff’s help in
promoting pro-green building policies and announced that AB 920 now requires that the electric
companies in California pay solar providers for their excess energy. In the past we were not able
to roll over the surplus dollars. She congratulated the Diablos and Mustangs football teams, both
champions in their divisions, and she encouraged residents to get out to the stadiums to watch the
playoff games beginning on Friday. Council Member Schlicht requested that the Mayor close
the meeting in memory of the thirteen who died in the Fort Hood shooting.

Mayor Pro Tem MacLean

Mayor Pro Tem MacLean asked staff to look into the lease that we pay the Santa Margarita
Water District for the corporate yard facility. If the land is in fact surplus property, he expressed
an interest in finding out what opportunities might allow us to have our own corporate yard. He
also asked staff to look into the cost of updating the freeway signs because they list an inaccurate
population for the City. Mayor Pro Tem MacLean wished everyone a happy Thanksgiving and
encouraged residents to enjoy family and time together.

Mayor Ury

Mayor Ury announced that he attended the Oxford Preparatory Academy presentation to the
Saddleback School District. He was very impressed with the level of detail and the proposed
programs and he was also pleased to see the time that the Trustees devoted to the discussion. He
noted that he hopes the OPA moves forward and he congratulated all the parents and the people
at Oxford who worked so hard to put the proposal together. Mayor Ury announced that he was
unable to attend the Veterans Day ceremony last week but he expressed his appreciation to all

City Council Minutes  11  November 16, 2009
 veterans and he thanked Mayor Pro Tem MacLean for running the event. Mayor Ury also
wished everyone a wonderful Thanksgiving.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 10:25 p.m., there being no further business to come before the Council at this
session, Mayor Ury adjourned the meeting in memory of the thirteen Fort Hood victims, to
Monday, December 7, 2009, at 5:00 p.m.

__________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of December 7, 2009

City Council Minutes  12  November 16, 2009
